_comment: Five enterprise policies, seventeen clauses. SPEC §22.5, G-67, FR-41. Each clause carries ITS OWN WORDS and names the control questions it bears on. The alignment (`governs`) is AUTHORED DATA RATIFIED BY A HUMAN — never something a model decides while a page renders: a requester asking 'why am I being asked this?' is owed an authority, and an authority a model invented is not one. A clause with an empty `governs` is a COVERAGE GAP in the instrument, named rather than dropped. Policy text is quoted verbatim or not at all (§22.5).

breach_rule._comment: The deterministic pass. It stands alone with no model available (G-67).
breach_rule.why_unanswered_is_never_a_breach: Silence becoming non-compliance is the mirror image of the mistake never-guess exists to stop (§3.2.1).
breach_rule.why_na_is_never_a_breach: Judging a control out of scope is a position a person took; testing it is the reviewer's job, not the platform's to pre-empt.
breach_rule.why_replaces: One fact, one finding, and the richer of the two — a breach replaces the bare control gap rather than joining it.

clauses.text: Every individual who accesses a corporate system shall do so using an account uniquely attributable to that individual. Accounts shall not be shared between individuals under any circumstances, including for third-party personnel and for temporary engagements.

Privileged credentials shall be issued from an approved credential vault on a time-limited basis. Standing privileged access shall not be granted to any individual, internal or external, without a documented exception approved by the Chief Information Security Officer.
Privileged entitlements shall be reviewed and reconfirmed by the accountable system owner no less frequently than once each quarter. Entitlements not reconfirmed within that period shall be revoked.
Authentication to any system holding data classified Confidential or above shall require at least two distinct factors. This requirement extends to break-glass and emergency accounts.
Data classified Internal or above shall be encrypted in transit using current approved protocols, including on connections internal to the corporate network.
Data classified Confidential or above shall be encrypted at rest. This requirement applies equally to backup copies and to any copy held by a third party on the organisation's behalf.

Encryption keys shall be held in an approved key management service, separated from the data they protect, and rotated on a defined schedule. Keys shall not be stored in source code, configuration files or artefact repositories.
On termination of a third-party engagement, the organisation shall obtain written certification that all copies of its data, including derived and backup copies, have been destroyed.
clauses.coverage_note: No question in the pilot instrument asks about destruction certification at exit. This is a gap in what we ask, not a gap in the policy (§22.1 read backwards).

clauses.text: The security and privacy posture of a third party shall be assessed and documented before the engagement commences. An engagement shall not proceed on the basis of vendor-supplied marketing material alone.
Contracts shall oblige the third party to maintain a current register of its own material suppliers and to notify the organisation in advance of any change to that register.

For any third party processing data classified Confidential or above, the organisation shall hold either a current independent assurance report or an exercised contractual right of audit. Where delivery is performed from a location other than the third party's principal place of business, the assurance shall cover that location.
Every model deployed in support of a business process shall be recorded in the AI inventory before it is used in production, with a named accountable owner.
Where a model's output contributes to a decision affecting an individual, a competent person shall review and approve that output before it takes effect. Post-hoc review does not satisfy this clause.
Any model-driven capability shall be capable of being disabled by an authorised operator without requiring a code change or a release.
A measured performance baseline shall be established before a model-driven capability is released, and re-measured after any change to the model, its prompts or its retrieved sources.

A restoration from backup shall be performed and evidenced at least annually for every system supporting an important business service, and the elapsed time recorded against the agreed recovery time objective.
Backup copies shall be held in a location or account logically isolated from the system they protect, such that a compromise of that system cannot alter or delete them.
